## COMPRESSED HISTORY

## Rule

Crop the top-left **16×16** of the one-hot grid. Per color (channel), a cell is a
**solid 2×2-block anchor** iff the 2×2 to its bottom-right is entirely that color
(`Conv` 2×2 all-ones, pads BR `[0,0,1,1]`, `>3.5`). Count anchors per color,
**excluding background color 0** (`no_ch0`); the color with the most anchors is the
**dominant color `dc`** (LIVE keeps all ties via `count+0.5 > max`, but ARC-GEN has
**no ties** — see analysis). Dilate the `dc` anchors back to their 2×2 cells
(`Conv` pads TL `[1,1,0,0]`, `>0.5`). **Output**: kept cells → `dc`; every other
in-grid cell → color 0; beyond the 16×16 grid → blank. Pad back to 30×30.

Corpus facts (N=20000, `prototypes/_oracle_analysis.py`): **ties 0, blank cells in
16×16 0, content outside top-left 16×16 0**; 19713 grids have exactly one color
with solid blocks, **287 have two** (so dominance counting is genuinely required —
cannot shortcut to "the one color with any block"). numpy oracle == LIVE == ARC-GEN
truth, byte-exact, 0 mismatches.

## Algorithm sketch

See `prototypes/_oracle_analysis.py:oracle()` for exact numpy (matches LIVE bit-for-bit).
```
inner = x[:, :, :16, :16]                       # crop16
sum2  = box2x2(inner, pad_BR)                    # per-color 2x2 sum
tl    = sum2 > 3.5                               # solid-block anchors
cnt   = tl.sum(spatial); cnt[ch0] = 0           # per-color counts, drop bg
dc    = argmax(cnt)                              # dominant color (no ties)
keep  = dilate(tl[dc], pad_TL) > 0.5            # kept cells
out   = dc where keep else 0 (in-grid), blank beyond 16x16
```

## Don't-do log

- **Don't pad a 16×16 canvas with a sentinel just to kill edge 2×2 anchors** — a 2×2 anchor
  can only live in [0,15)² (its block spills outside the 16×16 grid at row/col 15), so work
  the mono/histogram/dilate planes at **15×15 via 4 direct overlapping slices** of the index
  map (`idx[:15,:15]` vs the 3 shifted windows). Byte-identical to the sentinel approach,
  drops `idx_pad` (289) and shrinks every anchor plane 256→225. This was the v3→v4 win (−629).
- **Don't keep the dilate mask 0/1 then recolor with a separate `Where`+`keep_b`** — bake `dc`
  into the mask *before* the `MaxPool` (`Where(bc==dc, dc_u8, 0)`); since only one color
  populates it, `MaxPool` propagates `dc` and the recolor is free. Drops the `keep_b` plane
  (−256). v4→v5 win. (Don't instead `Mul(dom, dc)` — that ADDS a plane, net worse.)
- **DON'T believe "MaxPool/Mul/ReduceX reject uint8" without checking the OPSET** — `MaxPool(tensor(uint8))`
  IS accepted by ORT at **opset ≥12** (rejected only at 10/11; that's where the stale note came
  from — see `_archive/task286`). The shared `ort_reality.md` MaxPool row and `techniques.md`
  already say ≥12 OK. The whole dilate/recolor runs in U8: `Where(dom_b,dc_u8,0)` → `MaxPool` →
  `out_idx` U8 directly, **no F16 cast** (v5 F16 path was −740 of pure overhead → 7426→6686, v5→v6).
  Lesson: trust the opset-keyed dtype matrix in `ort_reality.md`, not a one-line opset-blind
  don't-do note carried forward from an older graph.
- **Don't try a cheaper dominant-color detector than the histogram** — the generator
  (`task_91714a58.py`) plants ONE box but lets noise colors randomly form 2×2 blocks
  (15/1000 grids have two colors with blocks). LIVE takes the true argmax-of-2×2-anchor-counts;
  "any color with a block" / "color with ≥4 anchors" / bbox-fill all risk a hidden divergence.
  The `bc_i32` [225] int32 scatter (900) is the §8d acknowledged floor — keep it.
- **Don't trust the prompt's "20,480 B INT64 [1,10,16,16]"** — stale. The LIVE 58,031
  graph is already all-F16/bool (selective_f16 applied 2026-05-19). Measure first
